title: Skyline
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9291fe99b8f5ab50bdc680836a8f0a31d57bf035.png)

*Busch is actually sort of a campus of New Brunswick, so Little Keshstein had time to appreciate the Busch skyline. However, he can't really figure out whether some buildings belong to Busch or Livingston, so he naturally comes up with the following problem.*

You are given a function f(b)𝑓(𝑏) that represents the maximum skyline achievable for an array b of length m, defined as:

f(b)=max(min(bi,bi+1,…,bj)⋅(j−i+1)), where 1≤i≤j≤m.

Given an array a of length n, partition its elements into two nonempty subsequences x and y such that each element is contained in exactly one of x or y, and f(x)+f(y) is maximized.

A sequence x is a subsequence of a sequence a if x can be obtained from a by the deletion of several (possibly zero or all) elements from arbitrary positions.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤t≤104). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer n (2≤n≤7500) — the length of the array.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a1,a2,…,an (1≤ai≤n) — the elements of the array.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n2 over all test cases does not exceed 75002.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum value of f(x)+f(y) that can be achieved by partitioning a into two nonempty subsequences x and y.

## Note

In the third test case, one optimal partition is x=[a1,a3]=[2,2] and y=[a2,a4]=[1,4]. We can show that f(x)+f(y)=2⋅(2−1+1)+4⋅(2−2+1)=8. We illustrate below.
